Students’ solutions were seen to be methodical and clearly set out.
The standard of algebra was usually good, although a number of students made basic sign or manipulation errors.
Q01(a), most students started by manipulating 1 (9 10 ) x  to give 1 2 1 10 1 3 9 x         although a few incorrectly wrote 1 2 10 3 1 9 x         .
notes.display: Q01(a), most students started by manipulating $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(9-10x)}}$ to give $\dfrac{1}{3}\left(1-\dfrac{10x}{9}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ although a few incorrectly wrote $3\left(1-\dfrac{10x}{9}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

notes.quote: The majority were able to use a correct method for expanding a binomial expression of the form (1 )n ax  .
A variety of incorrect values of a such as 10 , 9 9 10  or 9 10 and n such as 1 , 2 1  or 2  were seen at this stage.
notes.display: A variety of incorrect values of $a$ such as $\dfrac{10}{9}$, $-\dfrac{9}{10}$ or $\dfrac{9}{10}$ and $n$ such as $\dfrac{1}{2}$, $-1$ or $-2$ were seen at this stage.

notes.quote: The majority of students expanded 1 2 10 1 9 x         to give 2 5 25 1 ... 9 54 x x    , but some forgot to multiply this by 1 3 to give the answer to Q01(a). Sign errors, bracketing errors and simplification errors were also seen here.
notes.display: The majority of students expanded $\left(1-\dfrac{10x}{9}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ to give $1+\dfrac{5}{9}x+\dfrac{25}{54}x^2+\ldots$, but some forgot to multiply this by $\dfrac{1}{3}$ to give the answer to Q01(a). Sign errors, bracketing errors and simplification errors were also seen here.

notes.quote: In Q01(b) most students multiplied (3 ) x  by their binomial expansion from Q01(a).

A small minority, however, attempted to divide (3 ) x  by their binomial expansion. Some students attempted to expand (3 ) x  by writing it in the form (1 )n k ax  . Other students omitted the brackets around 3 x  although they progressed as if “invisible” brackets were there.
notes.display: A small minority, however, attempted to divide (3 ) x  by their binomial expansion. Some students attempted to expand $(3+x)$ by writing it in the form $k(1+ax)^n$. Other students omitted the brackets around 3 x  although they progressed as if “invisible” brackets were there.

notes.quote: In Q02(a) most students applied the trapezium rule correctly in order to find the approximate area for R.
The most common errors were using an incorrect strip width of 0.4 or not rounding their final answer to 2 decimal places.

In Q02(b) a number of acceptable reasons were seen to explain how the trapezium rule can be used to give a more accurate approximation. These included; increase the number of strips, make h smaller or increase the number of x and/or y values used.
Incorrect reasons included; use more decimal places, use smaller values of x and/or y or use definite integration.

In Q02(c) the majority of students employed a method of integration by parts with 2 u x   and 2 d e , d x v x  although a minority multiplied out 2 (2 )e x x  to give 2 2 2e e x x x  prior to integrating.
notes.display: In Q02(c) the majority of students employed a method of integration by parts with $u=2-x$ and $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=e^{2x}$, although a minority multiplied out $(2-x)e^{2x}$ to give $2e^{2x}-xe^{2x}$ prior to integrating.

notes.quote: Common mistakes included sign errors when integrating or evaluating their final answer; or integrating 2 e x to give either 2 2e , x 2 e x or 4 e . x k
notes.display: Common mistakes included sign errors when integrating or evaluating their final answer; or integrating $e^{2x}$ to give either $2e^{2x}$, $e^{2x}$ or $ke^{4x}$.

notes.quote: In Q03(a) many students were able to differentiate correctly, factorise out dy dx , and rearrange their equation to arrive at a correct expression for the gradient function such as 4 2 10 2 2 4 dy y x dx y x      .
notes.display: In Q03(a) many students were able to differentiate correctly, factorise out $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, and rearrange their equation to arrive at a correct expression for the gradient function such as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{4y-2x-10}{2y+2-4x}$.

notes.quote: A significant minority, however, did not simplify this expression as required by the question. A minority did not apply the product rule correctly when differentiating 4 , xy  whilst a small number left the constant term of 10 on the right hand side of their differentiated equation.
notes.display: A significant minority, however, did not simplify this expression as required by the question. A minority did not apply the product rule correctly when differentiating $-4xy$, whilst a small number left the constant term of 10 on the right hand side of their differentiated equation.

notes.quote: In Q03(b) most recognised that the numerator of their answer to Q03(a) had to be set to zero and obtained 2 5 x y   or 5 2 x y   , but then a minority gave up at this point. Whilst most substituted their 2 5 x y   (or equivalent) into 2 2 10 2 4 10 x y x y xy      a significant minority who had problems with the resulting algebra found difficulty in reaching a correct 2 3 22 35 0 y y    or equivalent.
notes.display: In Q03(b) most recognised that the numerator of their answer to Q03(a) had to be set to zero and obtained $x=2y-5$ or $y=\dfrac{x+5}{2}$, but then a minority gave up at this point. Whilst most substituted their $x=2y-5$ (or equivalent) into $x^2+y^2+10x+2y-4xy=10$ a significant minority who had problems with the resulting algebra found difficulty in reaching a correct $3y^2-22y+35=0$ or equivalent.

notes.quote: Those who progressed this far were usually able to solve the quadratic equation to give both correct values of y.
A minority of successful students applied an alternative method of finding both values of x, followed by using 5 2 x y   to find both values of y.
notes.display: A minority of successful students applied an alternative method of finding both values of $x$, followed by using $y=\dfrac{x+5}{2}$ to find both values of $y$.

notes.quote: Those students who separated the variables correctly in Q07(a), were usually able to integrate at least one side of their equation correctly.

Common errors at this stage included integrating 1 5000 N  to give ln(5000 ) N  and omitting a constant of integration “ c  ”, whilst a number of students found it challenging to integrate ( 1) kt t  . Some students did not show sufficient steps in order to progress from ln(5000 ) ln N kt t c      to 5000 e kt N At    . Other students found it challenging to remove logarithms correctly and gave an equation such as ln 5000 e e e kt t c N      which was then sometimes manipulated to the answer given on the question paper.
notes.display: Common errors at this stage included integrating $\dfrac{1}{5000-N}$ to give $\ln(5000-N)$ and omitting a constant of integration "$+c$", whilst a number of students found it challenging to integrate $\dfrac{(kt-1)}{t}$. Some students did not show sufficient steps in order to progress from $-\ln(5000-N)=kt-\ln t+c$ to $N=5000-Ate^{-kt}$. Other students found it challenging to remove logarithms correctly and gave an equation such as $5000-N=e^{-kt}+e^{\ln t}+e^c$ which was then sometimes manipulated to the answer given on the question paper.

notes.quote: In Q07(b) many students wrote down two equations each containing A and k and attempted to solve them simultaneously.
Algebraic manipulation and dealing with exponentials caused problems for a significant minority of students.
Those who were successful in finding the exact values of A and k, usually achieved the correct answer of 4400 fish in Q07(c).
In Q08(a) the majority of students were able to apply a full method of setting 1 y  in order to find t and substituting t into 4sin x t t   in order to find k.
notes.display: In Q08(a) the majority of students were able to apply a full method of setting $y=1$ in order to find $t$ and substituting $t$ into $x=t-4\sin t$ in order to find $k$.

notes.quote: Only a minority of students found and applied 2 t    to give the correct answer of 4 . 2 k    The majority used values of t such as 2  and 3 2  leading to incorrect answers of 4 2 k    and 3 4 2 k    respectively.

The majority used values of $t$ such as $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ leading to incorrect answers of $k=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-4$ and $k=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+4$ respectively.
